# onpager_enrichment_dataset (Resource)

Manage one enrichment dataset, including its metadata, enabled state and complete row set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_enrichment_dataset" "example" {
  name        = "service_owners"
  description = "Explicit passive inventory of service ownership."
  enabled     = false
  rows = [
    { service = "checkout", owner = "commerce" },
    { service = "billing", owner = "payments" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Immutable dataset name, 1–128 ASCII characters matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`. Changing it replaces the dataset; a deleted name can be reused for a new UUID.
- `rows` (Set of Map of String, Sensitive) Complete set of string maps. An explicit empty set clears all rows; null is invalid. The server sorts and deduplicates rows, so order has no meaning. Up to 100,000 rows, 256 distinct nonempty field names (at most 256 UTF-8 bytes each), 4096 UTF-8 bytes per value, no NUL, and 10 MiB encoded request. Empty maps and empty string values are supported. Reading requires `enrichment_dataset_rows.read`; contents persist in Terraform state.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes without NUL. Omitted/null defaults to an empty string; an explicit empty string clears it.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether runtime enrichment may use this dataset. Defaults to `true`; `false` is atomic on create. Content publication while disabled preserves `false`. Current rules referencing the dataset can block disabling.

### Read-Only

- `configuration_version` (Number) Dataset management CAS version. Metadata, content and publisher-token writes advance this version independently of the row revision; stale writes return HTTP 409 and require a new plan.
- `current_revision` (Number) Immutable row-content revision selected by the current dataset. Refresh reads every page of this exact revision, without scanning revision history.
- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.

## Import

Import using the dataset UUID. Import reads metadata and the current immutable
row revision, including disabled datasets.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_enrichment_dataset.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_enrichment_dataset.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

## Lifecycle and state

This resource owns the dataset's metadata and complete row set. Changing the
immutable name replaces the dataset. Omitted or null `description` defaults to
an empty string, and an explicit empty string clears it. Omitted or null
`enabled` defaults to `true`. Disabled creation is atomic; publishing rows while
disabled preserves that state. Current rule references can block disabling.

Rows are a set of string maps. The API sorts and deduplicates rows, so order and
repeated identical rows have no effect. Empty maps, empty string values and an
explicit empty row set are valid; null maps, null values and non-string values
are invalid. Dataset contents are sensitive and persist in Terraform state. The
separate `enrichment_dataset_rows.read` grant is required for refresh, import
and verification after writes.

Updates and deletion send body `expected_version` from `configuration_version`.
Row-content revisions and `If-Match` are not used for concurrency control.
Metadata, content and publisher-token writes advance the configuration version.
Metadata and row updates are separate requests: committed metadata and its new
version are saved before changed rows are published. A later failure retains
committed partial state. A follow-up read of a concurrent newer version cannot
replace the provider's committed snapshot. HTTP 409 requires a new plan;
mutations are not retried with a newer version.

Refresh reads metadata and every offset page of the exact immutable
`current_revision`. Only confirmed dataset absence removes state. Row-read,
authentication, authorization, transport and malformed-response errors retain
it.

Destroy sends DELETE for the dataset UUID with its saved configuration version.
Current rule references can block deletion with `dataset_in_use` (HTTP 409);
remove those references explicitly. Failure retains state. Successful deletion
removes current configuration and revokes publisher tokens. Captured immutable
history and author records remain; the API can prune unused history. Publisher
credentials are outside this resource's scope.

## Permissions

Requires tenant grants `enrichment_datasets.read`, `enrichment_datasets.create`,
`enrichment_datasets.update`, `enrichment_datasets.publish`,
`enrichment_datasets.delete` and the separate sensitive-row grant
`enrichment_dataset_rows.read`. Create requires both create and publish grants.
Service accounts require explicit native role assignments. Scoped publisher
tokens are a separate credential type and cannot replace management credentials.
